newsitem.title: GERMANY: German mid-cap shares shine in dull bourse session.
newsitem.headline: German mid-cap shares shine in dull bourse session.

text.p: Germany's main DAX-30 index closed an uninspired bourse session just ahead on Monday, with any real buying interest held back by Wall Street's lower close on Friday and by the lack of any real market-making news.

The main excitement was in the M-DAX index of mid-sized German shares which were driven to record all-time highs after the index finally broke levels which had in the past proved difficult for the market to surpass.
The DAX-30 index of leading shares closed 4.22 points, or 0.13 percent, higher at 3,263.86, while March futures on the DAX moved 6.5 points to 3,267.5.

The M-DAX, which includes 70 shares of medium-sized capitalisation drawn largely from the construction and consumer goods sectors, rose 55.12 points or 1.64 percent to 3,414.52, briefly setting a new all-time high of 3,414.75.

In the main market, support came from the continuing strength of the dollar at 1.69 marks but no new impetus emerged from elections in the state of Hesse after the two main political parties both registered gains.
"The market is a bit confused -- everyone seemed to be a winner in the Hesse state elections and there is little news around to lift shares," said a Frankfurt trader.

"Everyone seems to be waiting around for some piece of data. There are German unemployment figures coming out (on Thursday) and there are U.S. jobless figures due out as well this week," said one trader.
The IBIS-DAX post-bourse electronic index later closed 2.30 points lower at 3,258.74 after Wall Street narrowed early losses in mid-session trade on Monday.
Dealers said they now saw little chance of a significant move upwards before the resumption of U.S. Federal Reserve chairman Alan Greenspan's congressional testimony on Wednesday.
"Overall the market is on hold and is looking with some trepidation towards America," said one trader.
Features on Monday included chemicals Hoechst AG and BASF AG, which rose 25 pfennigs to 71.85 and 20 pfennigs to 62.45 respectively.
Deutsche Telekom finished bourse trade higher, up 1.10 marks at 33.60, as dealers said the stock was responding belatedly to recent moves upwards in the wider index.

In the M-DAX, the rise was seen most obviously in building stocks such as Strabag Bau, which gained 18.30 marks to trade at 165 marks, benefiting from a combination of computer-driven buying and a broker recommendation.
